newsitem.title: INDIA: India cabinet panel defers sugar price decision.
newsitem.headline: India cabinet panel defers sugar price decision.

text.p: An Indian cabinet committee did not take up a proposed hike in levy sugar issue prices at a meeting on Wednesday, a government spokesman said.
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs had been expected to consider Agriculture Minister Chaturanan Mishra's proposal to raise levy sugar issue prices by 1.60 rupees per kg.

The levy sugar issue price is the rate at which the government sells sugar to the public distribution system. It varies from state to state. Mishra had proposed raising the price by 1.60 rupees in each state.
"The items related to levy sugar pricing were not taken up by the cabinet," the spokesman said.
United News of India quoted Mishra on Tuesday as saying federal subsidies would rise by 7.2 billion rupees if state-controlled sugar prices were not increased by 1.60 rupees per kg.
Sugar supplies and pricing in India are controlled by the government.
Millers supply 40 percent of their output to the government at below-market rates for distribution through government shops at subsidised prices.
